newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch say EMU must include France and Germany.
newsitem.headline: Dutch say EMU must include France and Germany.

text.p: The Dutch government sees French and German participation as essential to European economic and monetary union (EMU), Finance Minister Gerrit Zalm told a news briefing on the Netherlands' 1997 budget.
"The establishment of EMU will only be meaningful if at the very least Germany and France take part," Zalm said. "Otherwise I don't think EMU will be launched in 1999," he said.
Zalm added that he expected Germany and France to meet the EMU entry requirements.
The Netherlands was also confident of EMU entry, even though its public debt ratio was above the EMU target, he said.
The overall level of Dutch public debt is set to fall to 76.2 percent of GDP next year from 78.8 percent, but will still be markedly higher than the EMU entry target of 60 percent.
"My defence in Brussels will be that the (Dutch) public sector deficit is well below the targeted three percent (of GDP)," Zalm said.
A public sector deficit of 2.2 percent would help check the rise of public debt relative to GDP, Zalm said, adding "we have not finished reducing the deficit yet."
